replacements.old: [F6] **External input — relative TOP normal bundle.** Freedman–Quinn, Theorem 9.3A, printed137–141, supplies an actual rank-two normal vector bundle for a locally flat proper surface in a TOP four-manifold, relative to a supplied normal bundle near a closed subset, including a boundary collar. Its neighborhood embedding agrees with that germ after restriction. This is only the normal-bundle input; it does not assert a circle-map fiber or a Seifert hypersurface. The usual full-AC setting of the Statement is retained.
replacements.new: [F6] **External input — actual relative normal-bundle criterion.** Freedman–Quinn, original §9.3, Theorem 9.3A, printed p.137 (scan PDF143), states: if $N$ is a closed subspace of an ANR homology four-manifold $Y$, $Y\setminus N$ is a manifold, $N\times\mathbb R$ is a manifold, the specified local complement fundamental-group conditions hold (infinite cyclic when $\dim N=2$), and an actual normal vector bundle is given near a closed set $C\subset N$ containing $\partial N$, then there is a normal vector bundle which agrees with that given bundle on a neighborhood of $C$. The relative agreement is part of the existence conclusion, not an inference from uniqueness. In the 2013 reformatted edition this is §9.5, Theorem 9.7, printed pp.144–145/PDF158–159, https://archive.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/4789/2/FreedmanQuinn-TopologyOf4Manifolds-Reformatted2013.pdf. Its p.145 footnote warns that local $\pi_2$ vanishing may also be necessary; step 8.1 satisfies that stronger condition as well. Apply the criterion to the CLOSED doubled sphere in boundaryless $S^4$, with the actual seam-annulus bundle germ constructed there, not directly to $B^4$. This supplies only a normal vector bundle, not a circle-map fiber or a Seifert hypersurface. Full AC is retained.

replacements.old: 8.1 Now let $D$ be the arbitrary locally flat disk of the Statement. Apply the relative normal-bundle input [F6] with the actual boundary product germ in [F1]. Its oriented rank-two vector bundle over the disk is trivial. A global nonzero frame section gives a disjoint proper parallel disk, so its boundary has linking zero with $K$ by [F3]. Thus the induced boundary framing is the preferred zero framing. Any difference from the supplied zero-framed boundary trivialization has degree zero in $SO(2)$ and extends across the disk; adjust the global frame by that extension, and restrict the actual bundle neighborhood. This gives an actual framed TOP disk tube, with the prescribed product and angular marking on a smaller boundary collar. Its compact exterior $X$ is a TOP four-manifold. The same collared decomposition and integral Mayer–Vietoris calculation as in step2.1 give $H_1(X)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$, $H_i(X)=0$ for $i>1$, with boundary the actual zero surgery $M(K)$ and its marked inner $D^2\times S^1$. No smoothing of the disk or exterior is asserted. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F6, step 2.1, construct, algebra]
replacements.new: 8.1 Now let $D$ be the arbitrary locally flat disk of the Statement. First construct the actual boundary germ. The smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ has an oriented normal two-plane tube $\tau:K\times D^2_\delta\to S^3$: take the positive normal of the given smooth Seifert surface along $K$, complete it by the orientations of $K,S^3$, and use a uniformly small smooth tube over the compact circle, by the smooth inverse-chart/ODE construction [F2]. The matched disk and ambient product collars in the Given identify $D$ there with $K\times[0,\epsilon)\subset S^3\times[0,\epsilon)$. Thus $(q,t,v)\mapsto(\tau(q,v),t)$ is an ACTUAL rank-two normal-bundle germ over the entire boundary collar. No global TOP bundle is inferred from the Definition alone.  Double the standard ball and the collared disk to $(Y,N)=(S^4,D_+\cup_KD_-)$, where $N\cong S^2$. The tube doubles to the explicit product germ $K\times(-2a,2a)\times D^2_\delta$ for small $a>0$. Choose the CLOSED seam annulus $C=K\times[-a,a]\subset N$. This is the prescribed bundle on a neighborhood of $C$; restrict its fiber radius inside a slightly larger tube for the extendable-neighborhood convention. The doubled pair is locally flat: away from the seam use the given charts; at the seam its actual product chart is $(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2,\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\{0\})$.  Every hypothesis of [F6] is now literal. The ambient $S^4$ is a boundaryless smooth manifold and hence an ANR homology four-manifold; $Y\setminus N$ is an open four-manifold. The surface $N$ is closed, $N\times\mathbb R\cong S^2\times\mathbb R$ is a manifold and $\partial N=\varnothing$. Nested flat charts have complement homotopy type $S^1$; the local meridian maps give the infinite cyclic local fundamental group, and local $\pi_2=0$. Thus even the stronger condition in the reformatted erratum holds. The actual prescribed bundle near $C$ is the displayed product. Apply [F6] to obtain a normal vector bundle on $N$ whose embedding AGREES with that product on a smaller neighborhood of $C$.  Restrict to $D_+$. Near its boundary, agreement with the germ keeps the collar coordinate $t$ unchanged, so sufficiently short fibers stay in the original hemisphere. Away from a smaller seam collar, the zero section is a compact subset of the interior of that hemisphere; continuity and compactness give a uniform fiber radius whose image stays there. Choose a bundle norm equal to the product norm near the seam and shrink to the smaller of those radii. This gives an actual disk tube wholly in the original $B^4$, agreeing with the prescribed product on a smaller entire boundary collar. Relative agreement, not existence of some unspecified doubled tube, justifies restriction. Its oriented rank-two vector bundle over the disk is trivial. A global nonzero frame section gives a disjoint proper parallel disk, so its boundary has linking zero with $K$ by [F3]. Thus the induced boundary framing is the preferred zero framing. Any difference from the supplied zero-framed boundary trivialization has degree zero in $SO(2)$ and extends across the disk; adjust the global frame by that extension, and restrict the actual bundle neighborhood. This gives an actual framed TOP disk tube, with the prescribed product and angular marking on a smaller boundary collar. Its compact exterior $X$ is a TOP four-manifold. The same collared decomposition and integral Mayer–Vietoris calculation as in step2.1 give $H_1(X)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$, $H_i(X)=0$ for $i>1$, with boundary the actual zero surgery $M(K)$ and its marked inner $D^2\times S^1$. No smoothing of the disk or exterior is asserted. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, step 2.1, construct, algebra]
